A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniQueR and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding content can be matched despite table renumbering and page reflow.

before.justification: V1 reports original novel-view synthesis, camera-pose, efficiency, geometry, and ablation results, supplemented by qualitative reconstructions in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds RealEstate10K novel-view synthesis results and a point-map-only query-initialization ablation.

M1.justification: The query architecture, hybrid initialization, attention, Gaussian spawning, and post-optimization remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 3.3 explicitly omits LPIPS during Stage 2, whereas v1 describes an undifferentiated L1-plus-LPIPS loss. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an actual training-objective change or newly disclosed stage-specific detail.

E1.justification: V2 adds novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K, previously evaluated only for camera poses. Other dataset and task coverage is retained. The change from 'BlenderMVS' to 'BlendedMVS' corrects a name already given correctly in v1 Appendix A.

E2.justification: New Table 3 compares UniQueR against FLARE and AnySplat for RealEstate10K novel-view synthesis. FLARE previously participated only in camera-pose comparisons. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added RealEstate10K evaluation uses 150 randomly sampled test scenes, two input and two disjoint target views, with identical selections across methods. V2 also reports fixed Q=4096 during training, contrasting with v1 Appendix A's variable-query description; that description remains in v2's appendix, leaving the actual query schedule unresolved.

E4.justification: V2 Table 7 adds point-map-only initialization alongside the retained random-only and hybrid configurations, testing whether geometric grounding alone suffices. Existing depth, query-count, Gaussian-count, and model-capacity ablations, plus appendix qualitative analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average five input-view subsets for the existing sparse-view evaluations. Neither adds training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new RealEstate10K sample size changes evaluation design, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports RealEstate10K PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 20.50/0.672/0.196 for UniQueR, 18.93/0.615/0.226 for AnySplat, and 17.74/0.586/0.371 for FLARE. New point-map-only ablation results are 18.58/0.627/0.313. Retained benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged; efficiency ratios receive more precise rounding.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), Gaussian construction, and attention-complexity expressions retain their mathematical substance. The shared non-metric coordinate-frame discussion clarifies existing conventions; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction changes 'state-of-the-art' novel-view synthesis and geometric accuracy to 'comparable' performance. The abstract narrows its comparison from state-of-the-art methods to recent baselines. The central query-based reconstruction and efficiency contributions remain, and the conclusion's broad improvement claim is retained.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges mixed VR-NeRF perceptual metrics and interprets the added initialization control. Its limitations expand beyond dynamic scenes to complex-scene underrepresentation, loss of high-frequency detail, and dependence on a large frozen backbone. It also clarifies that measured efficiency reflects the representation and decoder, not attention alone.

D1.justification: V2 specifies 12 Query Transformer layers, 502.31M trainable and 890.99M frozen parameters, loss weights of 0.1 and 0.2, and stage-specific loss usage. It identifies the ablations as Stage 1 and main NVS tables as Stage 2, and adds a project-page link. These disclosures supplement the largely unchanged implementation appendix.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the closest-prior positioning. It adds discussion of GS-LRM, LVSM, SceneTok, Point-DETR3D, LGM, AnchorSplat, and TokenGS, replacing the broad object-centric contrast with distinctions among explicit geometric queries, latent scene tokens, and scene-level Gaussian reconstruction. InstantMesh and Triplane Meets Gaussian Splatting are removed from the references.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites selected related-work, coordinate, initialization, training, and evaluation paragraphs for greater specificity while retaining the section hierarchy and overall narrative. Author affiliations, contribution footnotes, running headers, terminology, and citation assignments also receive localized edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds the RealEstate10K table, expands and relocates the ablation table, and reflows neighboring material. Several captions clarify evaluation stages or depth provenance, and Figure 5c gains an explicit parameter-unit label. The underlying figure images and plotted curves are retained.

improvement.justification: The added RealEstate10K comparison and point-map-only control strengthen empirical support. More specific prior-work positioning, training disclosures, and limitations improve interpretation of the retained results. These are limited gains: v2's fixed-query training statement conflicts with its unchanged appendix, and the stage-specific loss description does not establish whether training actually changed.
